goal: After this you can edit and search strings (append, substr, find, insert, erase, replace), compare strings, convert between text and numbers, use <cctype> functions and write small programs such as counting vowels, reversing a string and checking a palindrome.
warmup: Think of your WhatsApp name or a message you type: you add a word at the end, delete a mistake, search for a word in a long chat, change "Hello" to "Salam", or check whether two names are the same. A string in C++ can do every one of these with a ready-made function.
definition: The std::string class comes with member functions. A member function is called with a dot after the string: s.length(). Positions are called indexes and start at 0. find returns the index of a match, or the special value string::npos ("no position") when nothing matches. The header <cctype> adds simple functions that work on ONE character: isalpha, isdigit, toupper, tolower. The functions stoi and to_string convert between text and numbers.
howItWorks: Follow the trace of the first example and watch s change. append(text) adds at the end and push_back(ch) adds one character. substr(start, count) gives a COPY of a piece; the original is unchanged. find(text) gives the index of the first match. ALWAYS compare with string::npos before using the answer: if (s.find("x") != string::npos) means found. insert(index, text) puts text before that index. erase(index, count) removes characters. replace(index, count, text) swaps a part for new text. empty() is true for a string with no characters. COMPARING: you can use ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= directly on strings. They compare letter by letter by ASCII code, so "apple" < "banana", and "Zebra" < "apple" because capital letters have smaller codes than small letters. a.compare(b) gives a negative number, 0 or a positive number (rely only on its sign). CHARACTER FUNCTIONS (<cctype>): isalpha(c), isdigit(c), toupper(c), tolower(c). They work on one char, so use them inside a loop over the string. CONVERTING: stoi("42") gives the int 42 and to_string(43) gives the text "43". stoi expects digits; text such as "abc" cannot be converted. PATTERNS: count vowels (loop, tolower, compare with a, e, i, o, u); reverse a string (build a new one with rev = ch + rev, or swap the characters from both ends); palindrome (a word equal to its own reverse, such as level or Madam if you ignore case).
syntax:
string s = "Hello";
s.append(" World");        // Hello World
s.push_back('!');            // Hello World!
s.substr(6, 5);             // "World" (start, count)
s.find("World");            // 6, or string::npos if missing
s.insert(5, ",");            // Hello, World!
s.erase(5, 1);              // remove 1 char at index 5
s.replace(0, 5, "Salam");   // change first 5 chars
s.empty();                  // true if length is 0
a == b;  a < b;  a.compare(b);   // comparison

#include <cctype>
isalpha(c); isdigit(c); toupper(c); tolower(c);

int n = stoi("42");          // text -> number
string t = to_string(n + 1); // number -> text

explanation.text: append(text) adds text at the end (s += text does the same).
push_back(ch) adds one character.
substr(start, count) returns a piece of the string.
find returns a size_t index.
npos means not found. Always compare find's result with it.
insert(index, text) adds text before that index.
erase(index, count) removes characters.
replace(index, count, text) swaps a part of the string for other text.
empty() tells whether the string has no characters.

steps.note: s starts as Hello. Index: H0 e1 l2 l3 o4.
append adds text at the end.
push_back adds ONE character at the end.
substr(start, count): from index 6 take 5 characters. Index 6 is the W of World. s itself is not changed.
find returns the index where World starts: 6.
xyz is not in s, so find returns the special value string::npos. The if is true.
insert(index, text) puts the text BEFORE index 5, so a comma goes after Hello.
erase(index, count) removes 1 character at index 5: the comma is gone.
replace(index, count, text) swaps the first 5 characters (Hello) for Salam.
empty() is true (printed as 1) when the length is 0.

compare returns a negative number when a is smaller, 0 when equal, a positive number when bigger. We only test the sign.
Comparison uses ASCII codes: every capital letter (Z is 90) is smaller than every small letter (a is 97).

Make the letter small so that A and a are treated alike.

Builds the reversed lowercase copy.
A palindrome reads the same both ways. == compares the two strings.

variations.when: Add one character at the end.
Take a piece. Leaving out count takes everything from start.
Change a part of the string.
Check for an empty string (better than length() == 0).
Compare two strings by ASCII (dictionary) order.
Convert text to int, or a number to text.
variations.example:
int n = stoi("42");
string t = to_string(n);

mistakes.error: No compiler error. When the text is not found, find returns string::npos (a huge number), and using it as an index is wrong. Always check against string::npos first.

mistakes.wrong:
string a = "cat", b = "Dog";
if (a < b) cout << "cat first";   // expects true
mistakes.right:
// make both the same case before comparing
if (a[0] == 'c' && tolower(b[0]) == 'd') ...
mistakes.error: No compiler error, but the result may surprise you: comparison uses ASCII codes, so capital letters (D is 68) come before small letters (c is 99). The test a < b is false here. Convert both words to the same case before comparing.
Not a joined string: adding a number to a quoted text with + does not append the digits (it only moves along the characters of the text, which is a bug). Convert the number with to_string first.
A string and a single char are different types. Compare a character of the string (s[0]) with the char.

mistakes.wrong: s.erase(5);   // thinking this removes ONE character
mistakes.right: s.erase(5, 1);   // remove exactly one character at index 5
mistakes.error: No compiler error, but erase(5) with one argument removes everything from index 5 to the end of the string.

examTips: Remember the pattern: function(index, count, text): insert(index, text), erase(index, count), replace(index, count, text), substr(start, count).
find returns string::npos when nothing matches. Write: if (s.find(x) != string::npos).
Comparing strings uses ASCII codes: capitals before small letters; shorter prefix before longer word ("app" < "apple").
For count vowels / reverse / palindrome write a for loop from i = 0 to i < s.length(). To build a reversed string use rev = s[i] + rev.
stoi: string to int. to_string: number to string. The character functions need #include <cctype>.
romanSummary: append() aur push_back() string ke aakhir mein cheez jorte hain; substr(start, count) ek hissa nikalta hai; find() index deta hai ya string::npos agar na mile.
insert(index, text) beech mein jorta hai, erase(index, count) mitata hai, replace(index, count, text) badalta hai, empty() batata hai string khali hai ya nahi.
Strings ko ==, <, > se compare kar sakte hain; ye ASCII code ke hisaab se hota hai, is liye capital letters small se pehle aate hain.
<cctype> ke functions: isalpha, isdigit, toupper, tolower (ek character par). stoi text ko number banata hai, to_string number ko text.
Vowels ginna, string ulta karna aur palindrome check karna sab loop se hota hai jo s.length() tak chalta hai.

practice.hint: Count the characters before Fund, including the space.
practice.explanation: Programming has 11 letters (index 0-10), the space is index 11, so Fund starts at index 12.

practice.hint: Do the three changes in order.
practice.explanation: erase removes the space: HelloWorld. insert puts - at index 5: Hello-World. replace changes the first 5 characters (Hello) for Bye: Bye-World.

practice.prompt: What does s.find("z") return when s has no z?
options: -1 as an int you can print safely
practice.explanation: find returns string::npos when the text is not found. Check for it before using the index.

practice.hint: Compare ASCII codes: Z is 90, a is 97.
practice.explanation: Capital letters have smaller ASCII codes than small letters, so Zebra < apple is true.
stoi converts text that holds digits into an int.
isdigit needs a single character, so pass s[i], not the whole string. Also include <cctype>. The count for a1b22 is 3.

practice.prompt: Write code that reverses the string s into a new string rev using a loop.
practice.hint: Put each new character in FRONT of rev.
practice.explanation: Each character is added before everything collected so far, so the last character of s ends up first.

quiz.prompt: Which function adds one character at the end of a string?
quiz.hint: Think of pushing to the back.
quiz.explanation: push_back(ch) adds a single character. append adds text.

quiz.prompt: Which header is needed for isalpha and toupper?
quiz.explanation: The character-classification functions are declared in <cctype>.

quiz.prompt: What does s.substr(2, 3) give for s = "abcdefg"?
quiz.explanation: Index 2 is c, so the 3 characters are c, d, e.

quiz.prompt: Which is true about stoi and to_string?
options: stoi turns text into an int and to_string turns a number into text
quiz.answer: stoi turns text into an int and to_string turns a number into text

quiz.prompt: A word is a palindrome when...
options: it reads the same forwards and backwards
quiz.answer: it reads the same forwards and backwards
quiz.explanation: Compare the word with its reverse. If they are equal, it is a palindrome.
